newsitem.title: GERMANY: BDI says Bonn tax plan would bring investors - paper.
newsitem.headline: BDI says Bonn tax plan would bring investors - paper.

text.p: Bonn's planned cuts in corporate taxes were an "encouraging signal" that could draw investment needed to restart Germany's growth and jobs engine, the head of the Federation of German Industry (BDI) said in an interview.

"It is not today's tax conditions but those that are to be expected which attract investors," BDI President Hans-Olaf Henkel said in an interview appearing in business daily Handelsblatt on Wednesday.
"If clear signals are set, as the government now plans, investors will again come to Germany," he said.

Henkel also said BDI applauded the ending of tax-free holiday, Sunday and nighttime pay, but opposed a possible increase in the value-added tax. A VAT rise could put a brake on economic growth, he said.

The massive tax reform plan proposed cutting the top corporate income tax rate to 35 percent from 47 percent. Bonn was also considering raising the value-added tax by one percentage point to help offset the revenue reduction.
